subject: body
title: Growing Up
about: How a first grader grows: feet, legs and arms getting longer, height measured at a yearly checkup and the growth chart, why a baby tooth wiggles and when the first one usually falls out, learning new skills by practice, what the body needs to grow (sleep, food, play), babies to kids to teens to grown-ups, and the kind truths that everyone grows at their own speed and nobody can rush it. NC 1.PCH.1.3 (baby teeth give way to permanent teeth), 1.ICHR.1.2 (what makes each person special), 1.NPA.2.1 (activities good for the body) and Science LS.1.1.1 (what living things need to grow); the checkup and growth-stage cards are a bridge topic. Read it together: every question and choice is read aloud.
tip: Find his baby pictures and a shoe he has outgrown. Ask what has changed and what he can do now that he could not do then.

cards.q: Last year's shoes feel tight on your feet. What happened?
cards.note: Growing feet need a bigger size about once a year. A shoe store can measure them.

cards.q: Your pants that fit last winter are too short now. Which part of you grew?
cards.note: Legs do a lot of the growing at your age. That is why pants get short before they get tight.

cards.q: At a checkup, the doctor stands you against a measuring stick. What is being measured?
cards.note: Height is how tall you are. Most first graders grow about two inches in a year.

cards.q: Your coat sleeves stop above your wrists this winter. Which part of you grew?
cards.note: Arms and legs do most of the growing at your age. Grown-ups buy coats a little big so you can grow into them.

cards.q: The doctor draws a dot on a chart at every checkup. What does the chart show?
cards.note: A growth chart connects the dots from baby to now. Doctors like to see a steady climb.

cards.q: How often do healthy kids go to the doctor for a checkup?
cards.note: A well visit checks your growing, your eyes and ears, and your shots, even when you feel fine.

cards.q: A baby tooth gets wiggly. What is pushing up under it?
cards.note: The new tooth melts away the baby tooth's root, so the baby tooth comes loose and falls out.

cards.q: About how old are most kids when the first baby tooth falls out?
cards.note: Some start at five, some at seven. Both are normal.

cards.q: Which teeth do you keep for your whole life?
cards.note: Grown-up teeth are also called permanent teeth. Brush them well, they have to last.

cards.q: Babies learn to move in an order. Which usually comes first, crawling or walking?
cards.note: Most babies crawl first. Some scoot on their bottoms and go straight to walking.

cards.q: When you were a baby, riding a bike was too hard. How did you learn new things like that?
cards.note: Growing up means learning: walking, talking, reading, tying shoes. Practice does it.

cards.q: Which three things does your body need most to grow well?
cards.note: Sleep is when a lot of growing happens, food is the building material, and play makes bones and muscles strong.

cards.q: Some kids grow fast and some grow slowly. Is that okay?
cards.note: Bodies grow on their own schedules. Short, tall, early, late, all of it is normal.

cards.q: Baby, kid, then what comes next, before grown-up?
cards.note: Teenagers are 13 to 19. Teens grow fast and need lots of sleep too.

cards.q: Can you make yourself grow faster by trying really hard?
cards.note: Growing happens a little every day. Good food, sleep and play are all you can do.

cards.q: When do people stop growing taller?
cards.note: Most people reach their full height near the end of the teen years. Then you are done growing up, but never done learning.
